purpose: The state shapes LexLean applications declare, counted to choose which proved building blocks std-apps ships first.
method: Every state structure and every recursive helper (recursive_argument, mutual, or prim list_fold) is counted once per shape it fits; one declaration can count in several shapes. Counts are read from declaration headers of every file and approximate to about two.

lexlean-examples.where: examples/*/src of this repository, excluding the 90 certificate fixtures of uor-atlas and semantic-1.1

reproved: verdant: four monomorphic copies of List.append
forge: hand-written searches over lists of records keyed by a Nat; no lemma
forge and verdant shortfall lemmas, verdant six excess lemmas, by exhaustive grids
forge: 76 closed transition vectors and no parametric preservation theorem
all closed theorems over fixed catalog data, decided
forge duplicate digit parsers in ForgeKernel and PrismR4

findings: Nat codes dominate: state is flat records of Nat fields, flags tested with =? 1, phases and answers as Nat constants; lists are List Nat or lists of records keyed by a Nat index.
No surveyed application uses the map type or the map primitives; every keyed lookup is a hand-written search, so Tables is a list of key and value pairs.
Forge's stateful modules prove only closed transition vectors; no application states a parametric step-preserves-invariant theorem, which Machine supplies once.
The re-proved generic facts are sums over a list after cons, append and remove-first, presence from a positive count, and truncated-subtraction facts; these are the lemmas of Lists and Counter.
The two most frequent shapes, list-forall validators and fuel-driven parsers, are closed checks over fixed data or byte scanners; they need no state lemma and are left out of this first package.
